It narrows the usual CV/NLP preparation lens to robotics-specific issues, making it useful as a structured entry point for people trying to understand what matters technically in VLA systems.

title: leggedrobotics/pace-sim2real
summary: PACE targets sim-to-real transfer for legged robots by systematically identifying actuator and joint dynamics using only standard joint encoders, rather than relying on specialized sensing or hand-tuned modeling. The repo is useful for making simulated legged-robot behavior better match hardware, especially where unmodeled drivetrain and joint effects are a major source of transfer failure.

extra.full_text: PACE: A systematic approach for sim-to-real transfer of legged robots, identifying actuator and joint dynamics with standard joint encoders.

title: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground
summary: MuJoCo Playground is an open-source library for training robot policies with GPU-accelerated simulation and carrying them toward sim-to-real deployment. It is useful as infrastructure for robot learning experiments where fast MuJoCo rollouts, scalable reinforcement learning, and transfer-oriented workflows matter more than hand-building the simulation stack from scratch.

extra.full_text: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for writing GPU-accelerated simulation and compute kernels, aimed at robotics, physics simulation, and machine learning workflows. It is useful when researchers want CUDA-level performance from Python while building differentiable simulations, robot environments, or custom high-performance operators without dropping fully into low-level GPU code.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: IsaacLab-Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable simulation layer for building robot-learning environments from interchangeable robots, objects, task setups, and scene configurations. It is aimed at quickly prototyping and scaling policy evaluation across diverse embodiments and environments, making it useful for testing whether learned robotic behaviors generalize beyond a single hand-crafted simulator setup.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: iit-DLSLab/sim2real-robot-identification
summary: Provides joint calibration routines for quadrupeds and manipulators aimed at reducing the mismatch between simulated and real robot kinematics. It is meant to make policies or controllers developed in Isaac Lab or MuJoCo transfer more reliably onto physical robots by identifying and correcting joint-level discrepancies before deployment.

extra.full_text: A joints calibration routine for quadrupeds and manipulators to facilitate sim-to-real transfer from isaaclab and mujoco to real robots

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lightweight sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement-learning agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution across several robot platforms, including Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101, and YAM, making it useful for teams that want a tighter, simpler path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for basic quadruped locomotion, aimed at training and testing policies across multiple robot platforms. It is useful as a starting point for legged-robot experiments because it includes the surrounding pipeline pieces researchers usually need: simulation-to-simulation transfer and paths toward sim-to-real deployment.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab
summary: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab is a tutorial-oriented codebase for training robot behaviors with reinforcement learning and imitation learning on ROBOTIS platforms. It is aimed at the practical path from simulated training to real robot deployment, with Sim2Real support for moving learned policies onto physical hardware.

extra.full_text: This repository provides tutorials for reinforcement learning and imitation learning using ROBOTIS robots, and supports Sim2Real functionality for deploying the learned policies on real robots.

title: showlab/Awesome-Robotics-Diffusion
summary: Awesome-Robotics-Diffusion is a curated index of recent robot learning papers that use diffusion models for robotics tasks. It is useful as a scan-friendly entry point into the area, grouping work on diffusion-based policies, planning, control, and related robot learning methods rather than presenting a single new algorithm.

extra.full_text: A curated list of recent robot learning papers incorporating diffusion models for robotics tasks.

title: facebookresearch/project_superdex
summary: SuperDex is a unified robotics simulation platform from Meta that combines a purpose-built physics engine, authoring tools, and a scalable reinforcement learning interface. It is aimed at dexterous robot learning workflows where researchers need fast simulation, controllable task setup, and VR-based teleoperation in one place, with more capabilities planned beyond the current release.

extra.full_text: SuperDex brings together a purpose-built physics engine, robotics authoring tools, and a scalable reinforcement learning interface in a unified simulation platform, with VR-based teleoperation and additional capabilities planned for future releases.

title: wadeKeith/Awesome-Embodied-AI
summary: wadeKeith/Awesome-Embodied-AI is a curated index for embodied AI, collecting surveys, vision-language-action models, datasets, simulators, humanoid projects, robot learning resources, and safety material in one place. It is useful as a fast orientation map for researchers tracking the field, especially when comparing available model families, benchmarks, simulation environments, and adjacent safety work.

extra.full_text: Curated embodied AI list: surveys, VLA models, datasets, simulators, humanoids, robot learning, and safety resources.

title: dartsim/dart
summary: DART is a research-oriented C++23 physics engine aimed at robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings for easier experimentation. It is useful when a project needs simulation infrastructure for articulated bodies and robot dynamics rather than a black-box application layer.

extra.full_text: Research-focused C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings

title: menloresearch/isaac_asimov
summary: menloresearch/isaac_asimov is the official reinforcement-learning training framework for Asimov humanoid robots, built on NVIDIA Isaac Lab. It is meant for training and experimenting with humanoid robot policies in simulation, giving researchers a concrete Isaac Lab-based starting point for Asimov-specific locomotion or control work.

extra.full_text: Official reinforcement learning training framework for Asimov humanoid robots, built on Isaac Lab.

title: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy
summary: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy provides deployment code for taking robot policies from simulation into both sim-to-sim testing and real Deep Robotics hardware. It currently targets the M20 and Lite3 robots, making it useful as a bridge between trained control policies and practical validation on supported quadruped platforms.

extra.full_text: Sim-to-sim and sim-to-real deployment for Deep Robotics Robots, currently supporting M20 and Lite3

title: j3soon/ros2-essentials
summary: ros2-essentials packages a reusable ROS 2 stack for taking robot policies from Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab into physical deployment, with Isaac ROS components in the loop. It is aimed at sim-to-real robotics development where researchers want a common scaffold for training, testing, and deploying policies across simulated and real robots instead of rebuilding the ROS 2 integration each time.

extra.full_text: A reusable sim-to-real ROS 2 robotics stack for developing and deploying robot policies across simulation and physical robots, built around Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, and Isaac ROS.

title: engineai-robotics/engineai_rl_lab
summary: engineai_rl_lab collects Isaac Lab reinforcement learning environments for EngineAI’s PM01 and T800 robots. It currently targets whole-body tracking and adversarial motion prior training, making it a practical starting point for training and testing locomotion or full-body control policies on these specific robot platforms.

extra.full_text: This project provides a set of reinforcement learning environments based on Isaac Lab. It currently supports EngineAI PM01 and T800 robots, with implemented tasks including whole-body tracking and AMP.

title: AsterisCrack/BipedRobot
summary: A biped locomotion codebase built around Isaac Lab and MuJoCo, with custom implementations of PPO, SAC, DDPG, D4PG, and MPO for training walking policies. It supports MLP, LSTM, and Transformer policies, motion imitation, and sim-to-real workflows, making it useful as a practical sandbox for comparing deep RL controllers and deployment pipelines on legged robots.

title: castacks/AirStack
summary: AirStack is an agent-native framework for moving embodied AI from simulation to field robots with a closed-loop workflow that mirrors the target hardware one-to-one. Its emphasis is rapid sim-to-real deployment with self-validation, making it useful for robotics teams that need to iterate autonomy stacks against hardware behavior rather than treat simulation and deployment as separate worlds.

extra.full_text: Agent-native framework for rapid sim-to-real deployment of embodied AI for field robotics. Closed-loop, one-to-one workflow with hardware, self validating. Checkout develop branch for latest features.

title: open-edge-platform/physical-ai-studio
summary: Physical AI Studio provides an end-to-end imitation-learning pipeline for teaching robots from human demonstrations, covering the workflow from data collection through policy training and task execution. It is aimed at making physical AI development more practical for robotics teams that want to turn demonstrated behaviors into deployable robot skills without stitching together the full training stack themselves.

extra.full_text: Physical AI Studio is an end-to-end framework for training robots to perform tasks through imitation learning from human demonstrations.
